note.en: Valmiki opens the story by placing Kosala on the bank of the Sarayu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bala Kanda, Section V ("There is on the banks of the Sarayu a great and flourishing country called Kosala abounding in corn and wealth")

verification.notes: Relation read against dutt-ramayana Bala Kanda, Section V ("There is on the banks of the Sarayu a great and flourishing country called Kosala abounding in corn and wealth"); endpoints and type confirmed in the primary text.

note.en: Visvamitra tells Rama the Sarayu rises from Brahma's Manasa pool and flows past Ayodhya.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bala Kanda, Section XXIV ("the stream that issues from that liquid lapse, flows through Ayodhya: the sacred Sarayu issues from that pool of Brahma")

verification.notes: Relation read against dutt-ramayana Bala Kanda, Section XXIV ("the stream that issues from that liquid lapse, flows through Ayodhya: the sacred Sarayu issues from that pool of Brahma"); endpoints and type confirmed in the primary text.

note.en: The confluence of the Sarayu with the Ganga (Jahnavi) is heard by Rama mid-stream.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bala Kanda, Section XXIV ("as the Sarayu meets the Jahnavi, this tremendous uproar is heard, being produced by the clashing of the waters")

verification.notes: Relation read against dutt-ramayana Bala Kanda, Section XXIV ("as the Sarayu meets the Jahnavi, this tremendous uproar is heard, being produced by the clashing of the waters"); endpoints and type confirmed in the primary text.

note.en: Agastya directs Rama to Panchavati, describing it as lying near the Godavari.

note.en: Agastya names Panchavati and sends Rama there to build his hermitage.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Aranya Kanda, Section XIII ("Two Yojanas hence... known by the name of Panchavati. Repairing thither, do thou, rearing an asylum, pass thy time pleasantly")

note.en: Rama settles at Panchavati beside the Godavari on Agastya's instruction.

note.en: Surpanakha, mutilated, runs to Khara who holds Janasthana with his Rakshasa host.

note.en: Sugriva, exiled by Vali, lives on Rishyamukha with four companions.

note.en: Rama's first halt in exile is at Sringaverapura on the bank of the Ganga.

note.en: Visravas tells Kubera that Lanka stands on the brow of Mount Trikuta.
